fingerprint.hash_invalid_because: scores were recomputed by a different scorer than the one this fingerprint was built from; see derived.with

metric_descriptions.compression: Summary words divided by article words: a description, not a quality.
metric_descriptions.concision: ROUGE-Lsum precision over the whole summary: the share of what was written that matches the reference. Padding lowers it.

coverage.details: The summary is clipped to as many words as the gold summary has, then scored for ROUGE-Lsum recall against it (sentences split here, stemming on). Writing more cannot buy coverage; only putting the important facts first can. Read beside concision, which rewards the opposite.
coverage.summary: ROUGE-Lsum recall with the summary cut to the reference's length: did it carry the story.

metric_descriptions.fmt_bullets: 1 when the output has bullet lines where the prompt asks for sentences.
metric_descriptions.fmt_label: 1 when the output opens with a label such as "Summary:" the prompt did not ask for.
metric_descriptions.fmt_markdown: 1 when the output opens with markdown (bold, a heading, a quote) the prompt did not ask for.
metric_descriptions.fmt_narration: 1 when the output thinks out loud ("the user wants", "let me draft", think tags) instead of only summarising: its quality numbers describe something else.
metric_descriptions.fmt_overlong: 1 when the output runs past 90 words where the prompt asks for 2-3 short sentences.
metric_descriptions.fmt_paragraphs: 1 when the output has more than one paragraph where the prompt asks for 2-3 short sentences.
metric_descriptions.grounding: Share of the summary's distinct word bigrams that appear in the article: high is extractive, low means the summary left the source (a paraphrase or a fabrication).
metric_descriptions.input_truncated: 1 when a local model saw only part of the article, because it was longer than the model's encoder window (1,024 tokens for BART) and was cut, else 0. Those items are a different task from the hosted arms' full-article ones.
metric_descriptions.length_vs_reference: Summary words divided by reference words: 1 means as long as the human's. A verbose winner shows here.
metric_descriptions.reference_words: How many words the gold summary has.
metric_descriptions.rouge1: ROUGE-1 F1 against the reference, for comparison with published CNN/DailyMail results. Rises with length; read after coverage and concision.
metric_descriptions.rougeLsum: ROUGE-Lsum F1 against the reference (per-sentence longest common subsequence), the CNN/DailyMail literature's figure. Rises with length.
metric_descriptions.summary_words: How many whitespace-separated words the summary had.
metric_descriptions.truncated: 1 when the provider cut the reply off at the token ceiling (finish_reason "length", and in most adapters a completion that reached 98% of max_tokens), else 0. An arm with truncated above 0 has scores that partly describe the ceiling, not the model.
